title: Quantum Field Theory is the Ether renamed
summary: Why the vacuum is not empty, particles are field excitations, and non-locality points back to a connected medium.

body.heading: The vacuum is not empty
paragraphs: In general relativity, space is a geometric stage that can bend, but it is fundamentally empty. In quantum field theory the vacuum is a boiling, energetic sea, filled with zero-point energy and virtual particles. This is almost exactly what Tesla meant by a dense ether-like medium — modern physics calls it the quantum vacuum, but it functions as a physical medium with properties like permittivity and permeability.

body.heading: Particles as excitations
paragraphs: We don't treat particles as little billiard balls; they are localized excitations or ripples in a field. An electron is a vibration in the electron field — a mathematical version of Tesla's whirlpool in the ether. Excite the field and a particle appears; let the energy dissipate and it vanishes back into the field.

body.heading: Non-locality
paragraphs: Quantum entanglement is this phenomenon taken to its logical end: two particles, no matter how far apart, act as one. If the universe is filled with a single underlying medium, then distance is an illusion and the two are merely two points of the same fabric.

The name 'ether' was dropped largely for historical and political reasons. Michelson–Morley failed to detect a classical 'wind', and relativity was elegant without a gas-like medium. But when quantum mechanics brought the medium back, it used the language of 'fields' instead of 'ether'. Quantum field theory is the ether rebranded.
